# What two years of remote work did to our team

We went fully remote in March 2024 because our office lease ran out and the new one cost twice as much. Nobody planned it as a culture experiment.

The first six months were rough. Standups dragged on to forty minutes. Two people quit, one of them because she missed lunch with colleagues more than she expected. We tried "virtual coffee" on Fridays and dropped it after three weeks; nobody came.

What worked was boring: written decisions in one shared doc, and a rule that any meeting without an agenda gets cancelled. Our release cadence went from every three weeks to every two. I can't prove remote work caused that, but it didn't hurt.
